item.title: agentmemory: Persistent Memory for AI Coding Agents
item.description:
agentmemory is an open-source memory server that gives AI coding agents persistent memory across sessions. Hooks in Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw and other agents record what the agent does, and the server injects the most relevant past context when the next session starts. You install it with npx -y @agentmemory/agentmemory@latest.

The project lives at github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory, is written in TypeScript under the Apache 2.0 license, and had about 29,300 GitHub stars on 12 October 2026. This page covers what it does, how it works, how to set it up, what its benchmark numbers mean, and how it compares with Hindsight and Mem0 for coding-agent memory. Facts come from the agentmemory README and benchmark files, checked on 12 October 2026. (This site, aiagentmemory.org, has no connection to the agentmemory project.)

item.title: TencentDB Agent Memory: Layers, Team Memory, Setup
item.description:
TencentDB Agent Memory (repo TencentDB-Agent-Memory) is an open-source memory hub for AI agents from Tencent Cloud Database. It sits as a proxy between a coding agent and its LLM, saves each conversation, distills it into four layers (L0 to L3), and injects the right memory, skills, docs and code knowledge into every request. Its Team Memory release lets several agents and people share those assets with access control.

It is MIT-licensed, written mostly in TypeScript, and had about 27,900 GitHub stars on 12 October 2026. This page covers how its memory layers work, how to install it, what Team Memory adds, which agents it supports, and how it compares with Hindsight and Mem0. Facts come from the project’s README, INSTALL.md, CHANGELOG.md and SDK README, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs MemPalace: Extracted Facts vs Verbatim Recall
item.description:
Mem0 vs MemPalace is a choice between keeping facts and keeping everything. Mem0 sends each conversation to an LLM, pulls out short facts like “prefers Go,” and returns the matching ones on search. MemPalace saves conversations and files word for word on your machine and finds them later with local search, with no LLM and no API key.

Both are open source and among the most-starred memory projects on GitHub. They solve different problems: Mem0 is a memory layer for apps with many users, MemPalace is a personal, local archive built mostly for coding agents. Hindsight, an MIT memory server, covers ground from both: per-user banks for apps, native plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, a fully local mode, and the top answer-accuracy scores of the three on LongMemEval and BEAM. Facts below come from each project’s README, docs and PyPI page, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs Supermemory: Agent Memory APIs Compared
item.description:
Mem0 vs Supermemory is a choice between a memory-only layer and a memory-plus-context API. Mem0 extracts short facts from conversations and returns them by hybrid search, and you can run all of it yourself. Supermemory does fact extraction too, but bundles it with user profiles, document RAG and data connectors behind one hosted API.

Both have a free tier and paid plans from $19/month, and both can run on your machine, though in very different ways. Many teams comparing the two also look at Hindsight, an MIT-licensed memory server that scores highest of the three on LongMemEval and leads Mem0 by 9.8 and 15.5 points on the long-history BEAM 1M and 10M tests. This page compares all three on memory model, retrieval, self-hosting, benchmarks and pricing, using each project’s README, docs and pricing pages and Mem0’s own comparison pages, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs Hindsight: Agent Memory Layers Compared
item.description:
Mem0 vs Hindsight is a choice between two memory layers that sit beside your agent, not inside it. Hindsight does more work per memory: it links entities and time, merges facts into observations in the background, and can reason over them with reflect. Mem0 keeps memory lean: one LLM pass extracts facts, and search returns a small set of them cheaply.

The data splits along that line. On Mem0’s own comparison page, Hindsight leads by 9.8 points on BEAM 1M and 15.5 points on BEAM 10M, the long-history tests, and ships graph, temporal recall and consolidation in its MIT release, where Mem0 keeps them on its paid Platform. Mem0 returns about 4x fewer tokens per retrieval and lists SOC 2 and HIPAA for its Platform. This page compares them on memory model, retrieval, what’s free versus paid, benchmarks and cost, using each project’s README, docs and pricing pages, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Hindsight AI Memory: How It Works and When to Use It
item.description:
Hindsight is an open-source agent memory server from Vectorize, released under the MIT license with the full server included. It gives an AI agent three operations: retain (store and extract facts), recall (search memories) and reflect (reason over them to answer a question). It runs on PostgreSQL with pgvector, self-hosted or as the managed Hindsight Cloud.

Its strongest case is long histories: on the BEAM benchmark it scores 73.9 at 1M tokens and 64.1 at 10M, 9.8 and 15.5 points ahead of Mem0 by Mem0’s own comparison page. It also ships every feature (graph, temporal recall, consolidation, mental models, reflect) in the open-source release. This page covers how it works, what the benchmarks show, its real limits, and when another tool is the better pick. Facts come from the GitHub README, the official docs and the paper, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: MemPalace: Milla Jovovich's Open-Source AI Memory
item.description:
MemPalace is an open-source (MIT), local-first memory system for AI assistants, co-created by actress Milla Jovovich and developer Ben Sigman and released in April 2026. It stores your conversations and files verbatim, without summarizing them, sorts them into wings, rooms and drawers, and retrieves them with semantic search. Everything stays on your machine by default.

This page covers what MemPalace is, how its “palace” structure works, how to use it, and what its much-discussed benchmark numbers actually measure. Facts come from the MemPalace GitHub README and the official docs at mempalaceofficial.com, checked October 2026.

item.title: Letta Alternatives: 7 Agent Memory Options Compared
item.description:
Letta alternatives are memory systems you can use instead of Letta (formerly MemGPT) to give agents long-term memory. The main ones are Mem0, Zep, Graphiti, Cognee, LangMem, Hindsight and Supermemory. Most teams switch because they want a memory layer for their own agent, while Letta is now a full agent runtime that owns the loop.

This page covers what Letta does today, the common reasons to look elsewhere, a comparison table, a short section per option, and how to choose. For a deeper look at Letta itself, see the Letta guide.

item.title: Supermemory Alternatives: 7 Agent Memory Tools Compared
item.description:
Supermemory alternatives are other memory layers for AI agents: Hindsight, Mem0, Zep, Graphiti, Letta, Cognee and Honcho. People usually look for one when they need fully open-source, self-run infrastructure (Supermemory’s local server is a closed-source binary), want memory without bundled RAG and connectors, or need a different memory model such as a temporal graph or an agent that manages its own memory.

Below: what Supermemory does, a comparison table, a short section on each alternative, and how to pick. Facts come from each project’s README, docs and pricing page, checked on 8 October 2026.

item.title: Zep Alternatives: Open-Source and Hosted Options
item.description: Zep alternatives are other ways to give AI agents long-term memory: Graphiti (Zep’s own open-source core), Hindsight, Mem0, Letta, Cognee and Supermemory. Most people searching for one want a self-hosted, open-source option, because Zep stopped maintaining its Community Edition in 2025 and is now a managed, credit-priced service. Graphiti is the closest match to Zep’s model; Hindsight is the most complete open-source memory server, with graph and time-range recall, consolidation and reflect all in its MIT release.

item.title: What Is Mem0? How the Mem0 Memory Layer Works
item.description:
Mem0 (“mem-zero”) is an open-source memory layer for AI agents. It uses an LLM to pull durable facts out of conversations, stores them with embeddings per user, agent or session, and returns the relevant ones when you search. It ships as a Python and Node library, a self-hosted Docker server, and the managed Mem0 Platform.

This page explains how Mem0 works today, what changed in the April 2026 release, and how to configure, query and delete memories. Facts come from the Mem0 GitHub README, the Mem0 docs and the pricing page, checked on 8 October 2026.

item.title: Chatbot Memory on GitHub: Open-Source Repos (2026)
item.description:
Chatbot memory on GitHub falls into three groups: chat apps you self-host that already remember users (Open WebUI, LibreChat, LobeHub, SillyTavern), memory libraries you add to your own bot (Mem0, Letta, Graphiti, Memobase, Hindsight and others), and templates that show the pattern in a few files. Licenses range from MIT to AGPL to custom terms, so check before you ship.

Every repo below was opened and checked through the GitHub API on 8 October 2026. Stars are rounded and measure attention, not quality. For a deeper comparison of memory engines only, see open-source AI memory systems compared.

item.title: Mem0 Alternatives: 7 Agent Memory Tools Compared
item.description:
Mem0 alternatives are other memory layers that give AI agents long-term memory: Zep, Graphiti, Letta, Cognee, Hindsight, Supermemory and LangMem. Teams usually look for one when they need self-hosted graph memory (removed from open-source Mem0 in v3), temporal facts, an agent that edits its own memory, or different pricing.

For long histories, Hindsight has the strongest published numbers. Mem0’s own comparison page puts it 9.8 points ahead of Mem0 Platform on BEAM at 1M tokens and 15.5 points ahead at 10M, with the two level on LongMemEval.

item.title: Open Source AI Memory Systems Compared: GitHub Repos
item.description:
The leading open-source AI agent memory systems on GitHub are Mem0, MemPalace, Hindsight, Graphiti, Cognee, Letta, LangMem, MemOS, Memori, Honcho, Basic Memory and Memobase. Most are Apache-2.0 or MIT, written in Python, and self-hostable with Docker. They differ in storage (vectors, graphs, files), in how much is truly open versus paid, and in what they’re built for.

If you want the most complete fully open option, it’s Hindsight: its MIT server includes graph and temporal recall, consolidation and reflect, which Mem0 keeps on its paid Platform, and it leads Mem0 on the long-history BEAM benchmark by 9.8 points at 1M tokens and 15.5 at 10M (vendor-run). This page covers only open-source projects: repos, licenses, stars, languages and strengths. Star counts and licenses come from the GitHub API on 12 October 2026. For hosted options and benchmarks, see the LLM memory comparison. For background, see AI agent memory explained.
